_note: The decisive study: the question and protocol settled by the two pilots, fixed before the first hand. 1,000 hands (200 groups of 5), a fixed size: no stopping on results. Primary outcomes: Jev minus each language model on identical spots (estimate error; continue-or-fold accuracy). Expected cost about $45-50 at ~$0.045 a hand; the $60 cap is a safety limit above it, so the size, not the budget, ends the study. Rehearse free with --mock; --live spends real money and needs the user's go-ahead.

pilots.lesson: Jev was asked one question, and a pre-registered rule of ours moved its answer towards raising in 31% of its decisions; players had no hand facts. Jev was last against the pot actually won and made the fewest right decisions at identical spots. We dropped the rule: from then on, code changes no model's move.

With hand facts for every player, Jev asked in two parts (the kind of action, then the amount) and played exactly as it picked. Against Gemini 3.8 Flash and Llama 4 Maverick, its stated chances at identical spots were closer to the truth than both, while its decisions there trailed Gemini's; it won significantly more chips than both at a table where Llama's losses funded the winners. This study keeps that protocol and restores the full line-up of the first.
